title: Credential Emergency Handling and Audit Matrix
content:
Purpose:

This runbook captures a pragmatic, incident-ready process for emergency access (break-glass), ongoing rotation, and audit evidence capture for secrets used across Redwood Inference. It is intended to:
- Define clear, low-latency steps for teams to retrieve a credential in an outage while preserving auditability.
- Specify the minimal audit schema and SIEM mappings for secrets-related events so evidence can be correlated across systems.
- Provide an inventory schema and lightweight automation patterns for evidence export and retention.

Scope:

Applies to all machine/service credentials and high-privilege human credentials stored in our central secret store and approved vaults (HashiCorp Vault, cloud KMS-wrapped secrets). Excludes ephemeral per-request tokens that are already short-lived and have separate tracing.

Definitions and nomenclature: 
- Break-glass credential: pre-authorized emergency credential or retrieval path for high-impact services.
- Evidence bundle: time-stamped collection of artifacts (audit events, requester identity, command output, authorization ticket) captured and pushed to the SIEM for forensic use.
- Sealed snapshot: encrypted copy of a secret value escrowed with an access policy that requires multi-party attestation to unseal.

Roles and responsibilities:
- Security Ops (owner): maintain the break-glass inventory and validate audit schemas.
- On-call SRE/Platform Engineer: execute break-glass retrieval and rotate affected secrets after incident resolution.
- Service Owner (team): validate usage post-rotation, update credentials in config management, and run integration smoke tests.
- Legal/Compliance: notified for incidents involving secrets exfiltration; may require extended evidence retention.

Credential inventory schema (minimal fields):
- secret_id: human-friendly slug (string)
- classification: internal | restricted | confidential | regulated
- storage_backend: vault | gcp-kms | aws-secrets-manager | hsm
- owner: team name (string)
- last_rotation: YYYY-MM-DD
- rotation_cadence_days: integer (as string)
- break_glass: yes | no
- break_glass_holder: role or team (string)
- escrow_location: path or readonly link (string)
- audit_log_stream: syslog/appid/SIEM_index (string)
- credential_tags: comma-separated tags (string)

Recommended inventory practices:
- Enforce a single canonical inventory CSV/Sheet exported daily and validated by automation. Include a hash of the stored secret blob for tamper detection.
- Mark all break-glass credentials explicitly and limit by TTL and multi-party controls.
- Use escrowed sealed snapshots only for services with >48h RTO impact and document attestation flows.

Break-glass retrieval flow (short, actionable):
1) Initiation: The incident commander opens a JIRA incident ticket with severity and impacted service tags; tag: SEC-EMERGENCY.
2) Authorization: Security Ops on-call receives a Slack-approved 2-person approval (approvers listed in the inventory). Approval must be recorded as a Git shortlink or ticket comment.
3) Retrieval: On-call SRE runs the authorized retrieval script via bastion (example):
   vault read -format=json secret/data/service-x/emergency | jq -r .data.data.token > /tmp/sg-token
   The command MUST be run from an approved host with session recording enabled.
4) Evidence capture: Immediately run the evidence snapshot script which:
   - Collects the vault audit-event IDs for the read operation.
   - Captures requester identity, Slack approval permalink, and ticket ID.
   - Generates an encrypted evidence bundle and forwards to the SIEM ingestion endpoint with tag: emergency_evidence.
5) Usage and TTL: The retrieved secret is valid for a maximum of 2 hours by policy. After use, the service owner must rotate the credential (see rotation section).

Rotation and post-incident hygiene:
- If a break-glass retrieval occurred, rotate the secret within 2 hours of incident closure or revoke the token and issue a replacement.
- Rotation script example (HashiCorp Vault-backed):
   # rotate-secret.sh service-x
   export VAULT_ADDR=https://vault.internal
   new=$(vault kv put -format=json secret/data/service-x value=$(generate-secret) | jq -r '.data.version')
   echo "rotation_id:$new"
- Always update the canonical inventory last_rotation field and post a comment on the incident ticket containing rotation artifact links.

Audit log schema for secrets events (minimal required fields):
- event_id: GUID
- timestamp: ISO8601
- principal: user/service principal id
- action: create | read | update | delete | rotate | revoke | unseal
- resource: secret_id or path
- backend: vault | aws-secrets-manager | gcp-kms
- request_meta: client_ip, host, session_id (comma-separated key=val)
- approval_context: ticket=ID;approver=ids (if applicable)
- result: success | failure | forbidden
- change_summary: brief text (e.g., rotated to new_version 42)

SIEM export mapping and retention guidance:
- Map the audit schema fields to SIEM as top-level columns. Tag emergency flows with severity=high and evidence_bundle_id.
- Retain secrets-audit indices for 2 years for regulated tenants; default 90 days for internal low-risk secrets.
- Set an automated correlation rule: if action=read AND approval_context is empty AND principal classified as "human", generate an alert and create a high-priority ticket.

Evidence automation: capture pattern and artifacts:
- Trigger: completion of any action in {break-glass retrieval, rotation, revoke, unseal}.
- Artifacts to collect: audit_event_ids, command_history (session-recorded), approver permalinks, incident ticket id, host evidence (dmesg/ps for time window), and resulting secret version IDs.
- Packaging: evidence_bundle = tar.gz of artifacts + sha256sum, encrypt with KMS public wrapping key, post to SIEM endpoint with metadata JSON.
- Automation: small lambda/job listens to vault audit stream, aggregates events that match action set, and creates draft evidence bundles tagged for manual review.

RBAC v2 notes (secrets access):
- Principle of least privilege: generic roles should not contain break-glass permissions. Break-glass holders must be a dedicated role with MFA enforced and short session TTL.
- Role binding: prefer ephemeral role bindings (timeboxed group membership) via identity broker; avoid static IAM user memberships.
- Auditable policy changes: all policy modifications that alter secret access MUST be done via PR to infra repo and traceable back to a human author and ticket.

Incident playbook excerpt (for forensics team):
- Step 1: On alert of unauthorized secret read, snapshot SIEM events for 15 minutes before/after the read. Tag evidence_bundle with suspected exfil.
- Step 2: Freeze service credentials (revoke or rotate depending on impact).
- Step 3: Identify lateral activity by correlating session_id across logs (bastion, vault, app logs).
- Step 4: Notify Legal, engage incident response, escalate to execs if PII/regulatory risk.

Checklist (quick):
- [ ] Incident ticket created and labeled SEC-EMERGENCY
- [ ] Two-person Slack approval recorded
- [ ] Retrieval command run from recorded session host
- [ ] Evidence bundle created and uploaded to SIEM (evidence_bundle_id appended to ticket)
- [ ] Credential rotated and inventory updated

Open questions and proposals:
- Should break-glass secrets be constrained to single-use ephemeral tokens by default? Proposal: yes; migrate all break-glass creds to ephemeral short-lived vouchers within 6 months.
- Evidence retention policy alignment for regulated customers—confirm with Legal whether 2-year retention is sufficient for Europe-specific mandates.

References and helpful links:
- Vault audit log best practices (internal confluence link)
- SIEM ingestion schema and API (internal doc)
- Incident response runbook (IR team)

Notes to reviewers:
- This is intended to be operationally lean: prioritize low-latency retrieval while preserving a strong, queryable audit trail. Please comment on missing automation hooks or blockers tied to identity broker capabilities.

Author: Maya Thompson (security ops)
